clue.text: Excuse for swapping notes in test exercise

indicators.note: the musical notes A to G are letters, so one note-letter in the word is traded for another

parts.note: a test is an exam
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a way to get out of a test by passing notes around.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes here are musical: A to G are both note names and letters, so one vowel in the test word is traded for another.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to excuse or release them from a duty, a synonym in its verb sense.

clue.text: Clipping about TT race includes times

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take another piece inside them
about can mean round and around, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder for the rearrangement
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper cutting about the Isle of Man TT motorbike race lists the lap times.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is a famous motorbike race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipping cut from a newspaper is an extract, a passage taken out of a longer text.

clue.text: Online outlet with something going on?

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic, online things
a vent is an outlet for air or feelings

explanation.surface: An online shop, or a website for venting, wonders whether something is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, a happening, which is what something going on describes.

clue.text: Photograph cool playing of flute

indicators.note: playing with something moves it about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pic is short for picture
the letters of cool rearranged

explanation.surface: A photograph captures a laid-back musician playing the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small flute pitched an octave higher, so it is an example of the instrument.

clue.text: Weak charge left in live casing

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, with casing confirming the outer one wraps it

parts.note: to be is to live; casing marks it as the outer shell
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A feeble electric charge is left inside a live cable's insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means lacking strength, a straightforward synonym for weak.

clue.text: Learned to quarter, top and tail raw vegetables

indicators.note: topping and tailing vegetables cuts off both ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: east is one quarter of the compass
crudités are raw vegetables served as a starter

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: quarter the raw vegetables and trim their ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Crudités are sticks of raw vegetables served with dips; losing both ends leaves RUDITE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, pronounced as two syllables, means scholarly, and erudite is a synonym for well-read.

clue.text: Graduate takes on pupils, having aim to be writer

parts.note: a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
L is a learner, so two learners make pupils
the point of something is its aim

explanation.surface: A new graduate takes on a class of pupils, hoping to become a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, and writer here is a thing that writes rather than an author.

clue.text: Princess has massive lead cut coming back home in point-to-point

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the outer pair of letters

parts.note: two compass points, here east and east, form the outer shell

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: massive means huge

indicators.note: coming back means the next word is read from right to left

parts.note: at home is in

explanation.surface: A princess on horseback takes a commanding lead, then loses it on the way home in a point-to-point race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race over jumps; here it means two compass points enclosing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Eugenie is a granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, a royal named by her title.

clue.text: Dash of brown sauce coating young chicken

indicators.note: a coating goes all round something, so these letters wrap the next piece

parts.note: HP is a famous British brand of brown sauce
Y is an abbreviation for young
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A dash of brown sauce is drizzled over a young chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a bottled brown sauce found on British cafe tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a short dash used in writing to join words, so the punctuation mark fits.

clue.text: Walk taller?

parts.note: surface reading: go for a stroll
setter's reading: make one's lower limbs longer, an idiom for a stroll taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a short walk, taken literally, would make you taller by lengthening your limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go for a short walk after sitting for a while.

clue.text: Total endless organisation goes in to military display

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the following word
organising things puts them into a fresh arrangement
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the outer shell

explanation.surface: A military display is staged with total, unending organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' reads as a noun in the surface but works as the signal to rearrange TOTA, which then sits inside TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military show of marching and music, such as the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.

clue.text: They secure the locks for sharp bends

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clips that hold hair in place
second meaning: tight U-shaped turns in a road

explanation.surface: Something that secures locks is suited to sharp bends, like a security guard on a mountain road.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks here are locks of hair, not door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a U-shaped pin for hair and a very tight turn on a road, as in racing.

clue.text: Bob turns awfully obstinate

indicators.note: something done awfully is botched and jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Bob becomes terribly pig-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like the signal to rearrange, but it is part of the fodder; 'awfully' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and obstinate are synonyms, both meaning unwilling to change one's mind.

clue.text: Whole stilton,say, for head honcho?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: a large cheese, such as an entire round of stilton
second meaning: slang for the most important person in charge

explanation.surface: A whole stilton is suggested as the right gift for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Stilton is a blue English cheese sold in large rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means an important, powerful person, as does head honcho.

clue.text: Former French island has Democratic leader banished

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
île is French for island

indicators.note: 'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'Democratic'

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democratic

explanation.surface: A former French island has had a Democratic leader banished to it, like Napoleon on Elba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' tempts you to take a first letter, but Democratic is simply abbreviated to D.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiled means sent away from one's country, a synonym of banished.

clue.text: Fear for fellow Tory

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
the Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid for a fellow Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden fear, a close synonym.

clue.text: Regrouped, kicking out old gangster, then was in control

indicators.note: kicking someone out removes them, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: to regroup is to realign
Al Capone was the notorious 1920s Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gang regroups, throws out its ageing boss, and takes control.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule, so reigned is the past tense matching was in control.

clue.text: Catch some sleep between end of matinee and start of evening circus act

indicators.note: one piece sits between the two others, which surround it

parts.note: to trap is to catch

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of matinee
Z, as in catching some Zs, means sleep

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of evening

explanation.surface: A performer naps between the afternoon show and the evening circus performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapeze is a swinging bar used by acrobats, and the act performed on it is a classic circus turn.

clue.text: Support most important volunteers at home

parts.note: the main thing is the most important one
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: Volunteers who stay at home provide the most important support.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to support or keep it up, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Mummy's boy has unknown disease

parts.note: ma is mummy
a lad is a boy
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mother's son has a mysterious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z are the unknowns, so any of them can stand for unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, a slightly old-fashioned synonym for disease.

clue.text: Huge unregulated mines assimilate men without number

indicators.note: to assimilate is to take in, so the jumbled letters absorb another piece
without regulation things are disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Huge unregulated mines absorb workers without counting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without number' reads as 'countless' in the surface, but it tells you to drop a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, a synonym of huge.

clue.text: Reputation for being unhealthy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bad name, as in a house of ill repute

definitions.note: read cryptically as being famous for being sick
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: renown earned by being sick

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, splitting the phrase into sick plus celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means notoriety, a bad standing, mostly heard in 'house of ill fame'.

clue.text: Skid on Formula 1's Hungary track

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for formula
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
to tail someone is to track them

explanation.surface: A racing car skids on the Hungarian Grand Prix circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formula 1' looks like a single unit, but it is split into separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A car fishtails when its rear swings from side to side in a skid, like a fish's tail.

clue.text: Interfere with announcement of award

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a medal is an award

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with the announcement of a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in other people's business, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lived with upcoming pornographic model

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car
lewd means obscene

explanation.surface: Someone lived with a glamour model whose career was taking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, meaning lived somewhere, a synonym.

clue.text: Celebration for us on 18th birthday?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American national holiday on 4 July, with us read as US
second meaning, whimsical: the day a young person comes of age and gains freedom from parents

explanation.surface: Someone plans a party for the family on a child's eighteenth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'us' as US, the United States; the question mark flags the playful second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The American holiday on 4 July marks the 1776 declaration of freedom from Britain, and an eighteenth birthday brings adult freedom.

clue.text: Locomotive fails on elevated railroad

parts.note: an engine that fails dies
the El is an American overhead railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A train breaks down on an overhead railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a train engine powered by diesel fuel, so the word names a kind of locomotive.

clue.text: Sofa for solver?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: the person a crossword setter sets puzzles for

explanation.walkthrough: As an employer has an employee, a setter has a 'settee', the solver; the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a long upholstered seat for several people, a synonym of couch.
